title: Observability data lifecycle: quarantine pipeline + tenant provenance for traces and logs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our trace and log ingestion paths currently mix sensitive fields with operational telemetry. Customers have asked for: 1) a way to 'quarantine' suspect fields for manual review, 2) deterministic tenant provenance headers that survive sampling and aggregation, and 3) an enforcement layer that guarantees retention policy execution across Kafka -> warehouse -> short-term index stores.
rationale: Existing work focuses on redaction and retention, but we've seen incidents where automated scrubbing removed fields that downstream SRE/eval teams needed to troubleshoot. Quarantine provides a middle ground: isolate PII-like tokens in an access-controlled store and keep a lightweight provenance token in the main trace/log entry. This reduces data loss while preserving privacy controls and auditability.
scope: In scope: implement quarantine flag + quarantine payload store for traces/logs; add tenant_provenance header generation at ingress; extend retention enforcer to mark quarantined payloads with separate retention; RBAC for access to quarantine viewer UI/logs; audit logging for quarantine access. Out of scope: full UI for manual annotation (we will provide minimal viewer + CSV export), and long-term ML-driven PII detection (future work).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest pipeline adds 'quarantine' boolean and 'prov_token' (deterministic 128-bit hex) to trace/log JSON when a rule matches. 2) Quarantined payloads are stored in encrypted quarantine store (S3 prefix + KMS) with tenant_id tag and TTL metadata. 3) Retention enforcer honors separate TTL for quarantine store and will permanently delete objects after TTL. 4) Only users with 'observability.quarantine.read' role can access quarantine viewer endpoints; access events are logged to audit stream. 5) Integration tests simulate a PII-match rule and verify provenance token correlation between main index and quarantine store. 6) Performance overhead at ingestion is <6% p50 latency increase under 95th percentile load test.
proposed_solution: - Ingestion rules: extend current pipeline (kafka-ingest service) to run a lightweight deterministic matcher (regex + heuristics) producing 'quarantine' and 'prov_token'. Prov_token = HMAC_SHA256(tenant_id || ingress_ts || rule_id) truncated to 128-bit hex. - Quarantine store: new S3 prefix per-region with server-side encryption + object tags: tenant_id, prov_token, created_at, retention_policy. - Retention enforcer: extend existing retention job to scan quarantine prefixes and delete per-policy. - Access control: map existing SSO groups to new IAM role 'observability.quarantine.read'; add an audit hook that writes access events to the audit-kinesis stream. - UI: lightweight quarantine viewer service (read-only) that allows filtering by tenant/prov_token and exports CSV. - Tests: e2e test harness that verifies prov_token deterministic correlation and deletion flow.
implementation_notes: - Avoid storing raw PII in hot index. Main index entry must only include sanitized summary + prov_token. - Use streaming async writer for quarantine store to avoid blocking ingest; fallback to local durable buffer if S3 is throttled. - KMS key rotation: quarantine objects must survive key rotation — follow our KMS envelope patterns. - For prov_token generation use existing secrets service to fetch HMAC key; cache key for 1 hour. - Add feature flag 'quarantine-enabled' per-tenant to gate rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy on staging with synthetic traffic (2 days). 2) Canary: enable for 5 internal accounts for 48 hours to validate alerting and performance. 3) Ramp to 20% of production tenants (auto rollback on latency or error budget breach). 4) Full rollout after 7 days of stability. Provide runbook for rollback (disable feature-flag + drain quarantine writer).
migration_steps: - Backfill: not required for historical data; quarantine applies at ingestion. - For tenants that require migration, offer one-time reingest pipeline (separate ticket). - Ensure downstream dashboards are updated to include prov_token when available. - Update docs and notify on-call and SRE teams about new audit stream entries and quarantine viewer endpoints.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Metrics: quarantine_matches_total (by rule, tenant), quarantine_write_errors, quarantine_store_latency, prov_token_mismatch_count. - Dashboards: add per-tenant quarantine rate and cost estimate. - Alerts: >5% of traces quarantined for a tenant over 1h (possible regex explosion), quarantine write error rate >0.5% (S3/KMS issue), retention-enforcer failure. - Add replay debug view that, given prov_token, shows main index entry and quarantine payload correlation (read-only).
privacy_and_compliance: - Quarantine store encrypted with KMS key per-org. - Access to quarantine viewer subject to RBAC and SSO group mapping; every access emits an audit event with actor, tenant, prov_token, timestamp, and query. - Retention policies are tenant-configurable within allowed bounds; default quarantine retention is 90 days. - Security review required before full rollout (PCI/CCPA/GDPR checklist).

notes_for_code_reviewers: Look for potential performance regressions in kafka-ingest critical path. Confirm HMAC key usage doesn't leak into logs. Validate that prov_token algorithm is deterministic across instances and timezones. Ensure feature flag gating is comprehensive (ingest, writer, viewer).
